Tabelog not consulted: it has served Cf-Mitigated: challenge (HTTP 403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ THE 変わり蕎麦 SECTION IS WORTH UNDERSTANDING RATHER THAN JUST AVOIDING. This shop leads with 四色 at ¥2,000 — four soba in one order: さらし, 抹茶 (green tea), 胡麻 (sesame) and a seasonal one. Flavoured soba is made by working matcha, sesame or citrus peel into the dough, and because those additions weaken it the dough generally needs MORE binder, not less — so the coloured noodles a menu presents as the refined choice are, if anything, the more wheat-bearing ones. Nothing here publishes a ratio either way. ⚠ AND ONE ITEM IS BOTH NOODLES AT ONCE: うどん蕎麦合盛 at ¥1,200 serves soba and UDON on the same tray, which removes any doubt about wheat being in the kitchen. ⚠ THE PLATES WORTH KNOWING ABOUT: 板わさ (¥1,200) is fish cake, which is a quiet wheat item; こんにゃく味噌田楽 (¥850) is konnyaku, a plant, under miso; アボカド山葵 (¥850) is avocado and wasabi and is the closest thing here to a clean plant dish; and 蕎麦がき at ¥2,000 is buckwheat paste rather than noodles, which is the one form of soba with no dusting flour on it — worth asking about even though the ratio question remains.

⚠ そば味噌 is buckwheat groats roasted into MISO — plant in itself, and miso koji is sometimes barley, which is never declared. The nori is plant.
しらす are whole baby FISH; the daikon is plant and the dressing is soy.
The shop’s own description: a yolk steeped in 返し汁 — KAESHI, the concentrated soy base a soba shop builds its tsuyu from. Egg in soy.
Konnyaku is konjac yam — plant, and one of the few genuinely plant items here. The dengaku miso spread on it is the gluten-or-barley question.
Abura-age simmered in soy and mirin — plant in substance, and the simmering liquid is the wheat and possibly the dashi.

items.en: Pickles from a fifty-year nuka bed
items.note: ⚠ A REAL PLANT PLATE AND AN UNUSUAL ONE: vegetables from a 50-year-old rice-bran (ぬか) bed. Nuka is rice bran, not wheat, so a true nukazuke has no wheat route — the flag is an ask only because pickling beds are often adjusted with soy or sake lees.
Tempura in a dashi broth — wheat batter and bonito.
A dashi-based clear soup.

⚠ THE ONE FORM OF SOBA WORTH ASKING ABOUT. 蕎麦がき is buckwheat flour stirred with hot water into a paste — NOT rolled, NOT cut, so there is no 打ち粉 dusting flour and no shared boiling pot in the way there is with noodles. If the shop makes it from pure buckwheat this is the closest a soba house comes to a safe dish, and it is the question this record most wants answered. It is eaten with soy or with the shop’s soba miso, either of which reintroduces wheat.
A side egg; the cheapest item on the menu.
Glutinous RICE mochi, fried — no wheat in the mochi itself; the frying oil and any soy glaze are the questions.
